question: where did the error-driven allocation experiment's expensive artifacts go, was every upload verified against the local bytes before the local copy was released, and what does re-making each released artifact cost?
policy: docs/29 'Preservation: preserve before delete'. Upload first, re-verify the remote copy against the local bytes, and only then treat the local copy as expendable. tools/preserve_artifacts.sh never deletes: it prints the delete command and a human runs it.

model_repo.why_preserved: the candidate checkpoint of a measured negative: publishing the loser is what makes the hydrated recipe's win checkable by a third party, and the tree carries the exact per-module width maps, the pre-registered plan and the full conversion log with every realised proxy error
model_repo.recompute_cost: ~50 min of GPU for the conversion, on top of the 2 h 04 ladder pass that produced its input map -- or ~25 min with tools/allocate_bits.py --ladder-from-log against a conversion log that already exists

capture_error_driven.why_preserved: with the shard-0 BF16 reference already in this dataset, this capture lets anyone re-derive the headline paired number by `fidelity.py replay` alone: no GPU, no checkpoint
capture_error_driven.recompute_cost: ~6 min of GPU per 512-context capture (anchor: the surviving shard-0 BF16 capture's 170.08 s of prefill plus its model load), and only while the checkpoint still exists locally
capture_error_driven.file_digests_sha256_definition: sha256 over the sorted `sha256<two spaces>repo-relative-path\n` listing of every file in this upload -- the same text `sha256sum` would print. The per-file digests are not inlined because 513 hidden-state shards would be most of this receipt; regenerate the listing from the published tree and this digest checks it in one line.

capture_hydrated_rematched.why_preserved: the other operand of the same paired comparison, re-captured against the surviving BF16 reference with one harness version so the interval uses one reference and one code path
capture_hydrated_rematched.recompute_cost: ~6 min of GPU per 512-context capture; the published hydrated checkpoint still exists, so this one is recomputable, unlike a capture whose model is gone
capture_hydrated_rematched.file_digests_sha256_definition: sha256 over the sorted `sha256<two spaces>repo-relative-path\n` listing of every file in this upload -- the same text `sha256sum` would print. The per-file digests are not inlined because 513 hidden-state shards would be most of this receipt; regenerate the listing from the published tree and this digest checks it in one line.

ladder.why_preserved: the reusable artifact of the whole experiment: 409 modules x up to five widths with out_energy, numel, qmap and per-rung seconds. Everything in docs/37 section 3 is derived from this file
ladder.recompute_cost: 2 h 04 of GPU for the measurement pass (7,473 s, 2,000 module-quantizations). It is also committed verbatim at receipts/error-driven-ladder.json, so the dataset copy is convenience, not the only copy

what.recompute_cost: ~50 min GPU (or ~25 min via --ladder-from-log); downloading it from the Hub costs only wire time and is the cheap path
~6 min GPU, and only while the checkpoint exists locally

not_released.receipts/error-driven-ladder.json: 285 KB, committed verbatim and also published in the dataset. Nothing to reclaim.
not_released.the five allocation artifacts: solved-fixed.json, solved-override.json, plan-error-driven-allocation.json, build_solved.sh and convert-eda.log are now inside the model repo under allocation/, digest-verified at the same revision.

what_verification_means_here.remote-sha256-lfs-oid: the Hub's own LFS object id is a sha256 over the stored content, compared against the local sha256. End-to-end on the full bytes without re-downloading them.
what_verification_means_here.remote-git-blob-id: sha1 over 'blob <len>\0' + content, for files the Hub does not put in LFS.
what_verification_means_here.served-sha256-readback: the file was re-downloaded from the CDN and re-hashed: a claim about what the Hub actually serves, not only about metadata it computed.
what_verification_means_here.served-sha256-readback-lfs-spot: the same, for a spread sample of the LFS files. The model repo's sample was 1 of its 4 LFS files (one 8.5 GB shard); the other three are covered by their LFS oids. Each capture tree's sample was 3 of 512.
what_verification_means_here.problems: any missing file, size disagreement or digest disagreement exits non-zero and prints no delete command. All four uploads reported an empty problem list.

hardware: 1x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, SM120, driver 595.58.03, rental box. Every recompute cost above is that card's time and is not comparable to any other card.
